report_name: Unit 42 Develops Model to Map Cloud Identities via Behavioral Clustering

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The behavioral clustering model analyzes the activity of valid cloud accounts to establish baselines and detect misuse, which is central to identifying compromised valid accounts.

attack_patterns.name: Masquerading
attack_patterns.description: The model identifies masquerading threats by detecting when a cloud identity's behavior deviates from its established functional role, such as a service account performing actions typical of a human administrator.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Service Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The behavioral model provides context to determine if service discovery activities, such as an identity enumerating all resources, are benign (e.g., a security scanner) or malicious reconnaissance from a compromised account.

identities.name: Palo Alto Networks
identities.description: Parent company of Unit 42, which conducted the research on behavioral clustering.

identities.name: Unit 42
identities.description: The research group that developed and published the behavioral clustering methodology for cloud threat detection using AWS CloudTrail logs.

identities.name: Amazon Web Services
identities.description: The cloud provider whose AWS CloudTrail logs were used as the primary data source for the research.

indicators.name: Anomalous AWS Console Login by Non-Human Principal
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous AWS Console Login by Non-Human Principal
id: 2b8a1c9d-e4f3-4a1b-9c8d-7e6f5a4b3c2d
status: experimental
description: Detects AWS Management Console logins performed by non-human principals (e.g., AssumedRole, AWSService), which is highly anomalous and may indicate account misuse or masquerading.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/behavioral-clustering-map-to-cloud-identities/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-14
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
  - attack.t1036
level: high
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventName: ConsoleLogin
  filter:
    userIdentity.type: 'IAMUser'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects AWS Management Console logins performed by non-human principals (e.g., AssumedRole, AWSService), which is highly anomalous and may indicate account misuse or masquerading as a human user.

indicators.name: High-Risk IAM Modification
indicators.pattern:
title: High-Risk IAM Modification
id: 8d9e0f1a-2b3c-4d4e-b5c6-d7e8f9a0b1c2
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of new IAM users or roles, or the attachment of policies. When performed by an identity not designated for administrative tasks, this can indicate privilege escalation or persistence.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/behavioral-clustering-map-to-cloud-identities/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-14
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
level: medium
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventName:
      - 'CreateUser'
      - 'CreateRole'
      - 'AttachUserPolicy'
      - 'AttachRolePolicy'
      - 'PutUserPolicy'
      - 'PutRolePolicy'
    eventSource: 'iam.amazonaws.com'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of new IAM users or roles, or the attachment of policies. When performed by an identity not designated for administrative tasks, this can indicate privilege escalation or persistence through valid accounts.
